lottoParlays.writeup:
Expected script: Kansas City should ease Patrick Mahomes back from knee surgery with Kenneth Walker runs and quick throws to Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy. That also protects rookie left tackle Kahlil Benson, starting for injured Josh Simmons, from Nik Bonitto and Zach Allen. Denver is missing Jonathon Cooper, but its pressure unit still gives Kansas City a reason to avoid long-developing dropbacks.

Bo Nix's counter is Denver's clock-controlling short game: J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey on the ground, Courtland Sutton and Evan Engram underneath, then selective shots to Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims against a Chiefs secondary missing Chamarri Conner. Nix has completed 73.1% of his passes with seven touchdowns and one interception in four career meetings, but Steve Spagnuolo's disguised pressure should keep Denver patient.

The parlay's winning script is long drives, third-down battles and a one-score game near 20-20 in the fourth quarter. That favors Broncos +2.5 and Under 43.5 together. The danger is an early Waddle/Worthy explosive play, a defensive touchdown or Mahomes escaping pressure and forcing Denver into chase mode.
lottoParlays.fullAnalysis:
Kansas City's offensive plan should begin with risk management around Patrick Mahomes' return nine months after ACL surgery. Kenneth Walker gives Andy Reid a legitimate early-down runner who can create yards after contact, while quick-game targets to Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy can keep Mahomes out of obvious passing downs. The protection concern is real: starting left tackle Josh Simmons is out, leaving rookie Kahlil Benson to make his first career start against a Denver front led by Nik Bonitto and Zach Allen. Denver will not have Jonathon Cooper, so the rush is not at full strength, but forcing Kansas City to string together shorter gains still supports fewer possessions and the Under.

Denver's most likely answer is the same controlled passing structure Bo Nix has executed well against Kansas City. Nix completed 73.1 percent of his passes with seven touchdowns and one interception across four career meetings, and Denver produced 37 drives of at least 10 plays last season. J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey can keep the offense on schedule; Courtland Sutton and Evan Engram supply chain-moving targets; Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims provide selective vertical stress. Waddle also draws a favorable opportunity against a new-look secondary without safety Chamarri Conner, although his explosiveness is one of the Under's clearest failure points.

Steve Spagnuolo will disguise pressure and challenge Nix to identify Cover Zero and zone-pressure looks in Arrowhead noise. If Denver protects the football, stays ahead of the sticks and prevents Chris Jones from wrecking the interior, the Broncos should remain within one possession. The ideal parlay script is both teams leaning on quick throws and the run, long drives ending in field goals, and a score around 20-20 entering the fourth quarter. That makes each Denver point more valuable while keeping the total below 43.5. Explosive touchdowns, defensive scores or Mahomes creating off-schedule plays are the correlated ways both legs can fail.
